traits.smithy.api#documentation: The OAuth 2.0 grant type. Must be `client_credentials`.
The client ID of the OAuth application. Use together with `client_secret` as an alternative to HTTP Basic authentication.
The client secret of the OAuth application. Use together with `client_id` as an alternative to HTTP Basic authentication.
The OAuth 2.0 grant type. Must be `client_credentials`.
The opaque access token. Include it in the `Authorization` header of Users API requests as `Bearer <access_token>`. Access tokens begin with `op_o_c_`.
The token type. Always `Bearer`.
The lifetime of the access token in seconds. Access tokens expire after 15 minutes (900 seconds).
The scopes granted to the access token, separated by spaces. These are the scopes configured for the OAuth application, for example `users.view`, `users.suspend`, and `users.reactivate`.

Request an access token

Exchange the client credentials of an OAuth application for a short-lived access token,
using the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant.

Authenticate with the OAuth application's client ID and client secret in one of two ways:
send them in the `Authorization` header using HTTP Basic authentication (recommended), or
send them as the `client_id` and `client_secret` form fields. Use only one method per
request; a request that uses both is rejected.

A successful response returns an opaque bearer token that expires after 15 minutes
(`expires_in` is reported in seconds) and lists the scopes granted to the token, which are
the scopes configured for the OAuth application. Include the token in the `Authorization`
header of requests to the Users API as `Bearer <access_token>`.

Requests to this endpoint are rate limited per OAuth application and per 1Password account,
with limits shared across the token, introspection, and revocation endpoints.
A hint about the type of token. Optional; only access tokens are issued.
The client ID of the OAuth application. Use together with `client_secret` as an alternative to HTTP Basic authentication.
The client secret of the OAuth application. Use together with `client_id` as an alternative to HTTP Basic authentication.
The access token to introspect.
A hint about the type of token. Optional; only access tokens are issued.
Whether the token is currently active. `false` for tokens that are expired, revoked, unknown, or issued to a different OAuth application; the remaining fields are omitted in that case.
The scopes granted to the token, separated by spaces.
The client ID of the OAuth application the token was issued to.
The subject of the token. For client credentials tokens, this is the client ID.
The token type. Always `Bearer` for active tokens.
When the token expires, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.
When the token was issued, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

Introspect an access token

Check whether an access token is active and retrieve its metadata, following RFC 7662.
Authenticate with the client credentials of the OAuth application that the token was issued
to, using HTTP Basic authentication or the `client_id` and `client_secret` form fields.

The response always returns `200 OK`. An active token returns `"active": true` with its
scopes, client ID, and issue and expiry times. A token that is expired, revoked, unknown, or
issued to a different OAuth application returns `"active": false` with no other fields.

Requests to this endpoint share the token endpoint's rate limits.
A hint about the type of token being revoked. Optional; only access tokens are issued.
The client ID of the OAuth application. Use together with `client_secret` as an alternative to HTTP Basic authentication.
The client secret of the OAuth application. Use together with `client_id` as an alternative to HTTP Basic authentication.
The access token to revoke.
A hint about the type of token being revoked. Optional; only access tokens are issued.

Revoke an access token

Revoke an access token before it expires, following RFC 7009. Authenticate with the client
credentials of the OAuth application that the token was issued to, using HTTP Basic
authentication or the `client_id` and `client_secret` form fields, and send the token as
the `token` form field.

A successful request returns `200 OK` with an empty body. The endpoint also returns
`200 OK` if the token is already expired, revoked, unknown, or was issued to a different
OAuth application, so revocation requests are safe to retry.

Requests to this endpoint share the token endpoint's rate limits.

The 1Password OAuth API issues, inspects, and revokes the OAuth 2.0 access
tokens used to authorize requests to the 1Password Users API.

Integrations authenticate with the client ID and client secret of an OAuth
application in a 1Password account, using the OAuth 2.0 client credentials
grant (RFC 6749 §4.4). Access tokens are opaque bearer tokens that expire
after 15 minutes and carry the scopes configured for the OAuth application.
Tokens can be revoked before they expire (RFC 7009) and checked with token
introspection (RFC 7662). Refresh tokens aren't issued for the client
credentials grant; request a new access token when the current one expires.

All requests use `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. Responses
that return a body are JSON and include `Cache-Control: no-store` and
`Pragma: no-cache`, so tokens are never cached. A successful revocation
returns an empty `200 OK` response.
